# Product Spec: UX/UI Improvement — Ultron Dashboard

**Generated by:** Product Manager persona (Aitri pre-planning)
**Date:** 2026-03-03
**Status:** Ready for Architect

---

## 1. Core Problem Statement

Current state [a dashboard with percent-only metric tiles, no global alert indicator, and a 413-line settings scroll] causes [delayed system health assessment, missed alerts when not on the Alerts page, and navigation disorientation on mobile] for [Admin (sole Raspberry Pi operator)], resulting in [unnecessary cognitive load during daily monitoring and risk of missing critical hardware conditions].

---

## 2. Success Metrics

**Primary KPI:**
- All critical system health indicators (CPU, RAM, Temp with color state + absolute value) are visible above the fold on both 1080p desktop and 390px mobile viewport without scrolling — verified via visual inspection post-delivery.

**Guardrails:**
- Tailwind CSS build output increases ≤5% (enforced by purge config)
- Zero new Go route handlers required for Phase 1 (template-only constraint)
- All existing Go tests pass after template changes (`make test` green)
- SSE streaming behavior (metrics-cards, charts-area, ops-summary swap targets) unchanged

---

## 3. User Journey and Flow

### Happy path — Daily monitoring check
1. Admin opens dashboard URL → sees metric tiles with % + absolute values, all above fold
2. Admin scans tiles → color states (normal/warning/critical) give instant triage
3. Admin sees global alert indicator in header/topbar → zero alerts = no action needed
4. Admin navigates to Settings via sidebar → sees grouped sections (not one long scroll)
5. Admin adjusts a backup setting in its section → saves, returns to dashboard

### Failure / abandonment states
- **Alert fires while on Settings page:** Admin sees global alert indicator in header; navigates directly to Alerts
- **Mobile: sidebar hidden by default:** Hamburger tap opens sidebar; nav items have large touch targets (≥44px); active page is clearly highlighted
- **SSE connection drops:** Existing "Collecting data..." fallback tiles render — no new failure state introduced
- **Settings page tab spike fails (HTMX constraint):** Fallback to anchor-jump navigation (`#section-backup`, `#section-alerts`, etc.) within the same scroll — acceptable degradation

---

## 4. Scope and Guardrails

**In-Scope (Phase 1 — template changes only):**
- Metric tiles: add absolute value line below percentage (e.g., `1.2 GHz`, `1.8 GB / 4 GB`, `62°C`)
- Global alert indicator: persistent badge/dot in `base.html` header visible on all pages when active alerts exist; driven by same SSE event that powers sidebar badge
- Settings page: anchor-based section navigation (jump links: Backup, Telegram, Alerts, Hardware, Security, System) — no new routes
- Mobile nav: increase nav-item touch target to ≥44px height; ensure active-link state visible on mobile
- Timeline chips: increase font size from `text-[10px]` to `text-xs` (12px); add `title` attribute for screen readers

**Out-of-Scope (explicitly deferred):**
- Settings tabbed SPA behavior (requires new HTMX route design — Phase 2)
- New metrics or data sources
- Authentication page UX
- Chart visual redesign
- Accessibility full-audit (WCAG AA — separate initiative)
- External fonts or icon library changes

---

## 5. Acceptance Criteria

**AC-1 (Metric tile density):**
Given the dashboard loads with live SSE data, when the Admin views the metrics section, then each tile shows both a percentage value and an absolute value (e.g., CPU: `23.4% / 1.2 GHz`, RAM: `45% / 1.8 GB / 4 GB`, Temp: `62°C`) above the fold on a 1080p desktop viewport.

**AC-2 (Global alert indicator):**
Given one or more active alert conditions exist, when the Admin is on any page (Dashboard, Docker, Services, History, Logs, Settings), then a visible alert indicator (badge or dot) appears in the page header without requiring navigation to the Alerts page.

**AC-3 (Mobile navigation):**
Given the Admin accesses Ultron on a 390px viewport, when the sidebar is open, then each nav item has a minimum touch target height of 44px and the active page nav item is visually distinct (accent color or border).

**AC-4 (Settings navigation):**
Given the Admin is on the Settings page, when the page loads, then a navigation bar or jump-link list is visible at the top of the page showing the available sections (Backup, Telegram, Alerts, Hardware, Security, System) as anchor links, reducing the need to scroll blindly.

**AC-5 (No regression):**
Given all template changes are applied, when `make test` runs, then all existing Go tests pass with no failures.

---

## 6. Risk and Assumption Log

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Absolute metric values not available in SSE payload | Medium | High | Verify SSE payload structure in `sse-metrics.html` and Go SSE handler before implementing AC-1 |
| Global alert indicator driven by SSE — polling vs event | Medium | Medium | Reuse existing alert badge SSE event; extend to header element via same swap |
| Settings anchor nav adds 6 links above 413-line content — may push content below fold | Low | Low | Use compact horizontal pill nav with `position: sticky` |
| Mobile touch target increase may affect sidebar collapse animation | Low | Medium | Test collapse with expanded touch targets before delivery |

---

## 7. Dependencies and Constraints

| Item | Detail |
|---|---|
| Go SSE handler | Must expose absolute metric values in event payload (CPU frequency, RAM GB, Temp °C) — verify in `internal/metrics/reader.go` |
| Tailwind purge | All new CSS classes must be used in templates (not generated dynamically) to survive purge |
| HTMX SSE swap zones | `id="metrics-cards"`, `id="charts-area"`, `id="ops-summary"` — do not alter these IDs |
| `base.html` JS | Mobile hamburger toggle and sidebar collapse logic — read before modifying sidebar/header |
| No new Go handlers (Phase 1) | Settings section nav must work with existing `/settings` GET handler |
